name: Food trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about dishes, ingredients, cuisines, cooking terms. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which three vegetables make up the classic French flavor base called mirepoix?
items.explain: Mirepoix is a combination of onions, carrots and celery, used as a base for stocks, soups, stews and sauces.

items.question: In Cajun and Louisiana Creole cooking, the "holy trinity" uses bell pepper in place of which vegetable from French mirepoix?
items.explain: The Cajun trinity is onions, bell peppers and celery. The carrots of traditional mirepoix were swapped for bell peppers, partly because of availability and cost.

items.question: Which part of the Crocus sativus flower is dried to make the spice saffron?
items.explain: Saffron is made from the dried, golden-colored stigmas of the autumn crocus. Each flower has three of them.

items.question: Which compound gives saffron its rich golden color?
items.explain: Saffron contains a dye called crocin that gives food a rich golden color. Curcumin is the pigment in turmeric.

items.question: Which rice variety do most paella cooks use?
items.explain: Most paella cooks use bomba rice. A cultivar called senia is also used in the Valencia region.

items.question: In Spain, on which day of the week is paella traditionally included on restaurant menus?
items.explain: In Spain, paella is traditionally included on restaurant menus on Thursdays.

items.question: What happens to a roux's thickening power as it is cooked to a darker color?
answers: It increases as the flavor deepens
It decreases as the flavor deepens
It stays the same at every color
It increases as the flavor fades
items.correct: It decreases as the flavor deepens
items.explain: The darker a roux gets, the less thickening power it has. A chocolate roux has about one-fourth the thickening power of a white roux by weight.

items.question: A classic roux is made from what ratio of fat to flour by weight?
items.explain: Roux is typically made from equal parts of flour and fat by weight, cooked together to thicken sauces.

items.question: Which of these classic French sauces is NOT made with a roux?
items.explain: Roux is used in béchamel, velouté and espagnole. Hollandaise is thickened by emulsifying egg yolks and butter instead.

items.question: Which royal chef established the original four French mother sauces a century before Auguste Escoffier revised the list?
items.explain: Carême enshrined the original four sauces (velouté, béchamel, allemande and espagnole). Escoffier later added hollandaise and tomato and reclassified allemande.

source.title: The Mothers of All French Sauces

items.question: Béarnaise sauce, flavored with tarragon, shallot and white wine vinegar, is a derivative of which mother sauce?
items.explain: Béarnaise is made from hollandaise with tarragon, shallot and white wine vinegar added.

source.title: What Are the 5 Mother Sauces? And Their Derivatives

items.question: Which French mother sauce is made by adding milk to a white roux?
items.explain: Béchamel is built on a blonde white roux with milk added. Velouté and the other mother sauces use stock.

items.question: The browning reaction between amino acids and sugars that flavors seared meat and toast is named after which French chemist?
items.explain: The Maillard reaction is named after the French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard, who described it in the early 1900s.

source.title: Maillard reactions change the tastes of your food

items.question: Which ingredient, now standard in kimchi, was unknown in Korea until the early seventeenth century?
items.explain: Chili peppers are a New World crop and were unknown in Korea until the early 1600s. Earlier kimchi was not spicy red.

items.question: Kimchi was traditionally fermented and buried in the ground in ceramic pots known by what Korean name?
items.explain: In Korea, kimchi was fermented in traditional brown ceramic pots called onggi, often buried in the ground in winter.

items.question: Gazpacho, a cold soup of raw blended vegetables, is most closely associated with which region of Spain?
items.explain: Gazpacho, also called Andalusian gazpacho, is a cold soup from Andalusia in southern Spain.

items.question: Despite its name, what is gazpacho manchego?
items.explain: Gazpacho manchego is a meat stew served hot, not a variation on the cold vegetable soup.

items.question: Which nut forms the base of ajoblanco, the Andalusian "white gazpacho"?
items.explain: Ajoblanco is a cold soup of bread, almonds, garlic, water and olive oil, sometimes called white gazpacho.

items.question: Guanciale, the cured meat traditionally used in Roman carbonara, comes from which part of the pig?
items.explain: Guanciale is an Italian salt-cured meat made from pork jowl or cheeks. Its rendered fat flavors and thickens pasta sauces.

items.question: Most Italian sources trace the origin of pasta carbonara to which region?
items.explain: Most Italian sources place carbonara's origin in Lazio, the region around Rome.

items.question: What is the minimum aging period for Parmigiano-Reggiano?
items.explain: Parmigiano-Reggiano is a raw cow's milk PDO cheese aged at least 12 months. Most of it is sold at 24 to 36 months.

source.title: Parmigiano-Reggiano: How to Spot the Real DOP Wheel

items.question: Which herb is added during the production of Cypriot halloumi, giving it a slight minty flavor?
items.explain: Halloumi has a slight minty flavor because spearmint is added during production.

items.question: What does the French cooking term "sous vide" literally mean?
items.explain: Sous vide means "under vacuum." Food is vacuum-sealed and then slowly cooked in water at a low, controlled temperature.

items.question: From which seaweed did Kikunae Ikeda isolate glutamate in 1908, leading him to name the taste umami?
items.explain: In 1908 Ikeda identified glutamate, found in large quantities in kombu seaweed, as the source of the savory taste he called umami.

items.question: What plant is widely used in place of real wasabi in the paste served outside Japan?
items.explain: Real wasabi is costly and hard to cultivate. Western horseradish is widely used in its place.

items.question: Which genus of mold binds cooked soybeans together into a firm cake of tempeh?
items.explain: Tempeh consists of cooked and fermented soybeans bound together by the mycelium of Rhizopus oligosporus.

items.question: Tempeh, a fermented whole-soybean cake, originated in which country?
items.explain: Tempeh is a fermented soy food that originated in Indonesia, where it is still the most popular soy food.

items.question: Which flavor base of garlic, onion and peppers cooked in olive oil is common in Spanish and Latin American cooking?
items.explain: Sofrito is a base of garlic, onion and peppers cooked in olive oil, sometimes with tomatoes or carrots.

items.question: Traditional masa for tortillas is made by cooking and steeping dried corn in water mixed with which compound?
items.explain: Nixtamalization soaks corn in an alkaline solution, most commonly water mixed with calcium hydroxide (slaked lime, or cal). This softens the kernels so they can be ground into masa.

source.title: The ABCS of Nixtamal: Your Masa Guide

items.question: Soaking corn in an alkaline solution, as in nixtamalization, helps release which B vitamin from the kernel?
items.explain: The alkaline solution used in nixtamalization releases niacin (vitamin B3) from the corn kernel. This is why traditional tortilla-eating cultures avoided niacin deficiency.

source.title: The Process Of Nixtamalization, Explained - Tasting Table

items.question: Wilbur Scoville, who created the scale for measuring the heat of chili peppers, worked as what?
items.explain: Wilbur Scoville was an American pharmacist who devised his heat test in the early 1900s. He originally wanted to measure capsaicin for use in medicinal preparations.

items.question: In Scoville's original organoleptic test, a pepper extract was diluted in what until tasters could no longer detect any heat?
items.explain: The extract was diluted in sugar water until a panel of tasters could no longer detect heat. The degree of dilution gave the pepper's Scoville rating.

items.question: Which restaurateur is generally credited with creating the Caesar salad in Tijuana, Mexico, in the 1920s?
items.explain: The salad is credited to Caesar Cardini, an Italian immigrant who ran a restaurant in Tijuana. It is named after him rather than the Roman emperor, though some accounts credit his brother Alex.

items.question: In Liguria, which short, twisted pasta is the traditional choice to serve with pesto alla genovese?
items.explain: Trofie is a short, twisted pasta from Liguria that holds the sauce well. It is the traditional partner for Genoese basil pesto.

source.title: Authentic Pesto alla Genovese: How to Make Italian Basil Pesto - Love Italy

items.question: The name of the Ligurian sauce pesto reflects which kitchen action used to make it?
items.explain: Pesto takes its name from the idea of pounding. The traditional sauce is made by crushing basil, garlic, pine nuts and cheese in a mortar with a pestle.

source.title: Pesto alla Genovese (Italian Ligurian Basil Pesto)

items.question: Under the 1980 Bouillabaisse Charter, an authentic Marseille bouillabaisse must include which bony rockfish?
items.explain: The 1980 charter, drawn up by 11 Marseille restaurateurs, requires rascasse (Scorpaena scrofa). This bony rockfish lives in the calanques and reefs close to shore.

items.question: In a traditional Marseille bouillabaisse, which sauce is spread on garlic-rubbed bread served with the hot broth?
items.explain: Traditional Marseille service brings the broth first, with rouille spread on thick slices of bread rubbed with garlic. The fish is then served as a separate course.

items.question: Peruvian cevicherías often serve the citrus marinade as a drink called "leche de" which animal, literally "milk of" that animal?
items.explain: The marinade of lime juice, fish, onion, garlic and other seasonings is called leche de tigre, or "tiger's milk". It is often served in a small glass alongside the ceviche.

items.question: The cooking term "blanching" is named for the way the technique originally turned meat which color?
items.explain: Blanching was once used mainly on meat, which takes on a white hue when briefly soaked in boiling water. That effect gave the technique its name.

items.question: Blanching vegetables before freezing them helps deactivate what, which would otherwise degrade their flavor, color and texture?
items.explain: Briefly boiling produce deactivates enzymes that affect flavor, color and texture. This is why almost all vegetables are blanched before freezing.

items.question: Because its natural pollinators live only in Central and South America, how must most of the world's vanilla orchids be pollinated?
items.explain: Vanilla planifolia is pollinated naturally only by certain bees native to the Americas. Elsewhere, such as in Madagascar, hand pollination is required, which helps make vanilla one of the most expensive spices.

source.title: Section 4: Orchid Innovation: The Vanilla Orchid - Smithsonian Gardens

items.question: Roquefort cheese is made entirely from the milk of which breed of sheep?
items.explain: Roquefort is made only from the milk of Lacaune sheep. It is then aged in the caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon in southern France.

items.question: According to legend, a shepherd discovered Roquefort after leaving his lunch of bread and cheese in a cave to do what?
answers: Follow a girl he glimpsed far away
Chase a stray lamb across the hills
Shelter from a sudden mountain storm
Answer a bell ringing in the village
items.correct: Follow a girl he glimpsed far away
items.explain: The legend says the shepherd left his lunch to chase a beautiful girl he saw in the distance. When he returned months later, mold had transformed his cheese into Roquefort.

items.question: The pastry used in baklava is called phyllo, from a Greek word meaning what?
items.explain: Phyllo (or filo) comes from the Greek word for "leaf", describing the paper-thin sheets of dough that are layered to make baklava.

source.title: History of Baklava - Baklava by Wilma

items.question: What does the French cooking term "bain-marie" literally mean?
items.explain: Bain-marie comes from the medieval Latin balneum Mariae, meaning "Mary's bath". In the kitchen it is a pan of hot water that gently heats another container of food.

items.question: Roughly how many gallons of maple sap must be boiled down to produce one gallon of maple syrup?
items.explain: Maple sap is mostly water, so it takes approximately 40 gallons of sap to make one gallon of syrup. The ratio varies with the sap's sugar content.

items.question: Which tropical fruit ingredient is listed among the main components of Worcestershire sauce, alongside anchovies and malt vinegar?
items.explain: Worcestershire sauce is traditionally made with vinegar, anchovies, tamarind, garlic, onions and molasses. The tamarind adds a fruity tartness.

items.question: Which fungus is used as the kōji mold to ferment soybeans into miso?
items.explain: Miso is made by fermenting soybeans with salt and kōji, which is the fungus Aspergillus oryzae grown on rice, barley or soybeans.

items.question: Traditional haggis is made from sheep's "pluck". Which organs make up the pluck?
items.explain: Haggis is made from a sheep's heart, liver and lungs, mixed with onion, oatmeal, suet and spices. It is traditionally cooked in a sheep's stomach or a sausage casing.

items.question: Haggis is traditionally served as "haggis, neeps and tatties". What are the "neeps"?
items.explain: In Scottish cooking, neeps are mashed turnip or swede, and tatties are potatoes. Together they are the classic accompaniments to haggis.
